extracted.intended_audience: SABEW members and business journalists considering entry to SABEW awards or fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of eligibility, focus, and selection notes for SABEW's suite of awards and the Goldschmidt Fellowship program, intended for prospective entrants and nominators. Covers membership requirements, target work (e.g., business books), geographic-restricted contests, fellowship capacity, and discretionary awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best in Business Awards — membership eligibility and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: "SABEW celebrates the best in business journalism in an annual contest. It’s highly competitive and open to members in good standing at the date of entering. It typically runs December through early February."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must be SABEW members in good standing at time of entry; contest is annual and typically runs December through early February. Note: competition is described as "highly competitive."

rubrics_metrics.name: Best in Business Book Awards — focus on business books
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Best in Business Book Awards recognizing and celebrating outstanding business books is now open for submissions. SABEW is well-known for its prestigious Best in Business annual awards; this award focuses on business books as a standalone category."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be business books (standalone category). Purpose is to recognize and celebrate "outstanding business books."

rubrics_metrics.name: Canadian Best in Business Awards — Canadian membership restriction and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Canadian individual and institutional members can enter this unique contest just after the all-member contest closes in early February."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility limited to Canadian individual and institutional SABEW members; the contest opens immediately after the all-member contest closes (early February).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished Achievement Award — impact and mentorship criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: "Established in 1993, this award singles out individuals who have made a significant impact on the field of business journalism and who have served as a nurturing influence on others in the profession."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection criteria emphasize (a) significant impact on business journalism and (b) serving as a nurturing/influential mentor to others in the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goldschmidt Fellowships — program purpose and cohort size
rubrics_metrics.description: "The annual Goldschmidt Fellowship program provides a government data immersion experience for up to 20 Fellows. It is funded by the Chicago-based Walter and Karla Goldschmidt Foundation and 2026 marks the 12th year of this program."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship offers a government data immersion experience; cohort is limited (up to 20 fellows). Funded program with an annual cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: President's Award — discretionary selection
rubrics_metrics.description: "The President's Award is given by the current SABEW president at their discretion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is at the sole discretion of the sitting SABEW president; no stated formal eligibility or scoring criteria on this page.
